```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(pins)
library(reactable)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
library(htmltools)
library(here)

# dashboard/ is its own Quarto project, so tell {here} where this file sits
# relative to the repository root.
i_am("dashboard/index.qmd")

source(here("R", "ghgi_schema.R"))
source(here("dashboard", "R", "dashboard_data.R"))

schema <- read_ghgi_schema()
invisible(check_schema_links(schema))

# No pins board exists yet; the choice was deferred on 2026-11-20. An empty
# temporary board stands in for every home, so every dataset shows as not yet
# pinned. Replace these entries with the real boards once they exist.
empty_board <- board_temp()
boards <- c("agriculture", "energy", "ippu", "lulucf", "waste", "shared") %>%
  set_names() %>%
  map(function(home) empty_board)

as_of <- Sys.Date()

pin_dates    <- get_dataset_pin_dates(schema, boards)
pin_table    <- get_pin_date_table(pin_dates)
stages       <- get_dataset_stage(schema, pin_table, as_of)
stage_counts <- get_stage_counts(stages)
coverage     <- get_coverage_grid(schema, stages)
dependencies <- get_dataset_dependency_summary(coverage, stages)

# One blue scale, light to dark, for the ordered retrieval stages. Validated
# as an ordinal palette against the light chart surface.
stage_colors <- set_names(
  c("#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b"),
  retrieval_stage_levels()
)
ink_secondary <- "slateblue4"
gridline      <- "#e1e0d9"

# One accent per value box. Each passes 4.5:1 contrast against white text.
# Amber is kept for the overdue box so it reads as a call for attention.
box_colors <- c(
  datasets = "#3b4f6b",
  access   = "#0f766e",
  pinned   = "#1d4ed8",
  overdue  = "#b45309"
)

shared_stages <- SharedData$new(stages, key = ~dataset_id, group = "stages")
```

# Status {orientation="columns"}

## {.sidebar}

**Filters** apply to the table.

```{r}
#| label: filters
filter_select("f_stage", "Retrieval stage", shared_stages, ~retrieval_stage)
filter_select("f_provider", "Provider", shared_stages, ~provider)
filter_select("f_access", "Access method", shared_stages, ~access_method)
filter_select("f_home", "Home", shared_stages, ~home)
filter_select("f_dict", "Dictionary", shared_stages, ~dict_status)
filter_select("f_overdue", "Overdue", shared_stages, ~overdue_status)
```

To filter by source category, type part of a category name in the filter
box under the table's **Categories** column.

Built `r format(as_of, "%B %d, %Y")` from the schema in `schema/parquet/`
and the pins boards. Read only.

### Row {height="52%"}

```{r}
#| title: Datasets
stage_cell <- function(value) {
  dot <- span(style = str_glue(
    "display:inline-block;width:0.7em;height:0.7em;border-radius:50%;",
    "margin-right:0.4em;background:{stage_colors[value]};"
  ))
  return(span(dot, value))
}
date_col <- function(name) {
  colDef(name = name, format = colFormat(date = TRUE), minWidth = 110, na = "")
}
text_col <- function(name, min_width = 110) {
  colDef(name = name, minWidth = min_width)
}

reactable(
  shared_stages,
  searchable = TRUE,
  filterable = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 20,
  compact = TRUE,
  striped = TRUE,
  columns = list(
    dataset_id               = text_col("Dataset", 150),
    dataset_name             = text_col("Name", 240),
    provider                 = text_col("Provider"),
    access_method            = text_col("Access method"),
    home                     = colDef(name = "Home", na = "none"),
    n_categories             = colDef(name = "No. of categories", minWidth = 100),
    categories               = colDef(name = "Categories", minWidth = 260, na = ""),
    retrieval_stage          = colDef(name = "Retrieval stage", minWidth = 160,
                                      cell = stage_cell),
    cleaned_pin_state        = text_col("Cleaned pin", 120),
    raw_pin_last_created     = date_col("Raw updated"),
    cleaned_pin_last_created = date_col("Cleaned updated"),
    dict_status              = text_col("Dictionary"),
    calc_use                 = text_col("Used by calculation"),
    drift_status             = text_col("Drift"),
    update_frequency         = text_col("Provider releases"),
    overdue_status           = text_col("Overdue")
  )
)
```

# Coverage

## Row

```{r}
#| title: Coverage grid. Each cell is a category that uses a dataset, colored by the dataset's retrieval stage. Hover for details.
# Rows run by sector, then category name; columns by home, then dataset.
row_order <- coverage %>%
  distinct(sector, source_name) %>%
  mutate(row_label = str_c(sector, " · ", source_name)) %>%
  pull(row_label)
col_order <- coverage %>%
  distinct(home, dataset_id) %>%
  arrange(home, dataset_id) %>%
  pull(dataset_id)

# A stepped color scale: each stage gets one flat band of color.
n_stages <- length(stage_colors)
band_edges <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n_stages + 1)
stage_colorscale <- map(seq_len(n_stages), function(i) {
  list(list(band_edges[i], stage_colors[[i]]), list(band_edges[i + 1], stage_colors[[i]]))
}) %>%
  flatten()

coverage %>%
  mutate(
    row_label = str_c(sector, " · ", source_name),
    stage_num = as.integer(retrieval_stage),
    hover = str_c(
      "<b>", source_name, "</b> (", sector, ")<br>",
      dataset_id, ": ", dataset_name, "<br>",
      "Role: ", role, if_else(required, " (required)", " (optional)"), "<br>",
      "Dataset home: ", home, "<br>",
      "Stage: ", retrieval_stage
    )
  ) %>%
  plot_ly(
    x = ~dataset_id,
    y = ~row_label,
    z = ~stage_num,
    type = "heatmap",
    text = ~hover,
    hoverinfo = "text",
    colorscale = stage_colorscale,
    zmin = 0.5,
    zmax = n_stages + 0.5,
    xgap = 2,
    ygap = 2,
    colorbar = list(
      title = list(text = "Retrieval stage", side = "top"),
      tickvals = seq_len(n_stages),
      ticktext = names(stage_colors),
      len = 0.4,
      y = 1,
      yanchor = "top",
      outlinewidth = 0
    )
  ) %>%
  layout(
    xaxis = list(title = "", categoryorder = "array", categoryarray = col_order,
                 tickangle = -90, tickfont = list(size = 8), dtick = 1,
                 showgrid = FALSE),
    yaxis = list(title = "", categoryorder = "array", categoryarray = rev(row_order),
                 tickfont = list(size = 10), showgrid = FALSE, ticksuffix = "  "),
    font = list(color = ink_secondary),
    plot_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    paper_bgcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    margin = list(l = 10, r = 10, t = 10, b = 10)
  ) %>%
  config(displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

tagList(

# Dependencies

## Row

```{r}
#| title: Which categories depend on each dataset. Click a row to list the categories.
# The categories under one dataset, shown when its row is expanded.
dependency_details <- function(index) {
  this_dataset <- dependencies %>% slice(index) %>% pull(dataset_id)
  rows <- coverage %>%
    filter(dataset_id == this_dataset) %>%
    select(sector, source_name, role, required)
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(NULL)

  details <- reactable(
    rows,
    compact = TRUE,
    outlined = TRUE,
    pagination = FALSE,
    columns = list(
      sector      = colDef(name = "Sector", minWidth = 100),
      source_name = colDef(name = "Category", minWidth = 280),
      role        = colDef(name = "Role", minWidth = 160),
      required    = colDef(name = "Required", minWidth = 90,
                           cell = function(value) if_else(value, "yes", "no"))
    )
  )
  return(div(style = "padding: 0.5rem 1rem 1rem 2rem;", details))
}

reactable(
  dependencies,
  searchable = TRUE,
  filterable = TRUE,
  defaultPageSize = 25,
  compact = TRUE,
  striped = TRUE,
  details = dependency_details,
  columns = list(
    dataset_id      = colDef(name = "Dataset", minWidth = 160),
    dataset_name    = colDef(name = "Name", minWidth = 260),
    provider        = colDef(name = "Provider", minWidth = 120),
    home            = colDef(name = "Home", na = "none"),
    retrieval_stage = colDef(name = "Retrieval stage", minWidth = 160,
                             cell = stage_cell),
    n_categories    = colDef(name = "Categories", minWidth = 100),
    n_sectors       = colDef(name = "Sectors", minWidth = 90),
    n_required      = colDef(name = "Required by", minWidth = 100)
  )
)
```

# How to update

## Row

::: {.card title="Changing dataset details"}

Everything on this dashboard is generated from the CSV files in `schema/`.
Those files are the only thing you edit by hand; the Parquet files and this
dashboard are rebuilt from them. Full instructions are in
`how-to/maintain-the-schema.qmd`.

**Where each kind of change goes**

| To change | Edit |
|---|---|
| A dataset's provider, access method, endpoint, or other details | `schema/ghgi_datasets.csv` (one row per dataset) |
| Which categories use which datasets, and each link's role and required flag | `schema/ghgi_category_datasets.csv` (one row per category and dataset pair) |
| Dictionary status | `schema/ghgi_dictionaries.csv` |

**After each round of edits**

1. Rebuild and validate the schema:
   `source(here::here("R", "build_schema_parquet.R"))`.
   The script rebuilds the Parquet files and checks them against
   `schema/data-dict.yaml`. If anything breaks a rule, it stops and names the
   rule and the rows, for example a crosswalk row pointing to a dataset that
   does not exist, or a value that is not on the allowed list.
2. Re-render this dashboard: `quarto render dashboard`.
3. Commit the CSV files and the rebuilt Parquet files together, with a message
   saying what changed and why. The Git history is the record of changes.

:::

::: {.card title="Things to watch for"}

- **New allowed values.** If a new access method or provider is not on an
  allowed list, the build rejects it. Add the value to `schema/data-dict.yaml`
  first, then use it in the CSV.
- **Renaming a dataset ID.** Every crosswalk row that uses the old ID must
  change too; the build catches any you miss. Avoid renames unless you need
  one, because they break the link to earlier history.
- **Editing in Excel.** Convenient for large batches, but Excel can turn
  values into dates, drop leading zeros, or change the text encoding. Check
  `git diff` before committing.
- **Large batches.** Make them on a branch so the whole set of changes can be
  reviewed before merging.

:::
